title: ADR-01 Identity and envelope signing
outcome: How agents sign C1 envelopes without holding keys (signer handle), what the gateway verifies (sig, nonce, expiry, epoch, act chain), and what happens on failure; due 24 Nov
acceptance: ADR file ≤900 words with sections Context, Decision, Consequences, Interface touched (which of C1–C6), Tests that prove it
Decision: keys never enter the agent process; agent signs via a signer handle; agent + gateway signatures over the shared canonical serializer
Decision: a bad signature suspends the submitting connection, never the claimed agent_id; replayed/expired envelopes are denied and recorded
Tests listed map to RT2 (key theft), RT3 (forgery), RT4 (replay), RT6 (clock games)
summary: ADR-01 written (850 words): in-memory Ed25519 keys, signer handle over socketpair signing headers only, commit-then-sign with args_hash and shared canonical serializer, nonce/expiry_tick/epoch replay checks, act_chain with MAX_ACT_DEPTH used only for ancestor denial, 7-step verification order, bad sig suspends conn never claimed agent, SPIFFE ids as production mapping. Tests map to RT2, RT3, RT3b, RT4, RT6.
